learning_outcomes.text: Obtain an overview of the fundamental concepts of Computer Science, operating systems, and imperative programming.
Know the control structures of structured programming and basic data structures.
Learn to design algorithms to solve problems, selecting the most appropriate control and data structures in each case.
Be able to write programs in a specific programming language.
Build small and medium-sized applications, ensuring they are correct, efficient, well-organized, and well-documented.
Know the top-down design technique and concepts related to modularity.
Obtain an overview of the fundamental concepts of databases.
Strengthen critical capacity, mainly in the choice of methods for solving problems.
Work in a team and develop skills in arguing one's own ideas and justifying decisions.

syllabus_topics: Graphical representation of algorithms and their translation to C
Modules that do not return any value
Modules that return more than one value

assessment_methods.method: Student participation in various in-person and virtual activities (AE3)

assessment_rules: Two evaluation systems are available: continuous and global. For continuous evaluation, the final grade is calculated from an objective test (20%), a development test (60%), and participation in activities (20%). Participation activities (AE3) are not recoverable. To aggregate the grade, a minimum of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in both the objective test (AE1) and the development test (AE2); if a grade below 4/10 is obtained, points are subtracted from the final grade (1 for AE1, 2 for AE2, 1 for AE3). For global evaluation, the grade is based on an objective test (25%) and a development test (75%); if a grade below 4/10 is obtained, points are subtracted (1 for AE1, 3 for AE2). If a grade of 5/10 or higher is obtained in AE1 and/or AE2 in the ordinary call, it will be maintained for the extraordinary call of the same academic year.
